title: Generator congruences determine a local map and extend to fractions
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A,A'$ Noetherian commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $h:A\to A'$ be an $R$-algebra homomorphism, and let $\mathfrak p\subset A$, $\mathfrak p'\subset A'$ be prime ideals with $h^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak p$. Write $h_{\mathfrak p}:A_{\mathfrak p}\to A'_{\mathfrak p'}$ for the induced local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}:\widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}\to\widehat{A'_{\mathfrak p'}}$ for the induced homomorphism of maximal-ideal completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion-map-local]. Let $B=R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)$, with $n,m\geq0$ finite and the polynomial ring interpreted by iteration of [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime ideal. Suppose $\theta:B_{\mathfrak q}\to\widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}$ is a local $R$-algebra homomorphism, where local means that the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. Put $a_i=\theta(\overline T_i/1)$. Fix $N\geq1$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_n\in A'$ such that $F_j(b_1,\ldots,b_n)=0$ for every $j$, and, writing $\iota:A'_{\mathfrak p'}\to\widehat{A'_{\mathfrak p'}}$ for the completion map and $J=(\mathfrak p'A'_{\mathfrak p'})^N\widehat{A'_{\mathfrak p'}}$, suppose $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}(a_i)-\iota(b_i/1)\in J$ for all $i$.

There is a unique $R$-algebra homomorphism $\phi:B\to A'$ with $\phi(\overline T_i)=b_i$. For every polynomial $H\in R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$, one has $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}(\theta(\overline H/1))-\iota(\phi(\overline H)/1)\in J$. Moreover $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak q$, so $\phi$ induces a local homomorphism $\phi_{\mathfrak q}:B_{\mathfrak q}\to A'_{\mathfrak p'}$, and for every $z\in B_{\mathfrak q}$ one has $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}(\theta(z))-\iota(\phi_{\mathfrak q}(z))\in J$.

proof.text: Use the finite-sum polynomial evaluation of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] (the same finite monomials as the iterated polynomial ring) to define $e_b:R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\to A'$. Each $F_j$ maps to zero, so every finite sum $\sum_jG_jF_j$ maps to zero. Thus $\phi(\overline H)=e_b(H)$ is independent of the representative, preserves the ring operations and the $R$-structure, and sends $\overline T_i$ to $b_i$. Any other such map agrees on all polynomials by the cited universal property, hence on their quotient $B$. This proves existence and uniqueness, including empty generator or relation lists.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, proof: the map B to A′ and the marked-point conclusion, with the omitted algebra written out

proof.text: Put $C=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $D=A'_{\mathfrak p'}$ and let $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak n$ be their maximal ideals. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] these are local rings, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] applies to the complements of the respective primes, so both are Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] to each. Write $\pi_C:\widehat C\to C/\mathfrak m$ and $\pi_D:\widehat D\to D/\mathfrak n$ for coordinate one. Their kernels are precisely the maximal ideals $\mathfrak m\widehat C$ and $\mathfrak n\widehat D$. In particular $J=\mathfrak n^N\widehat D\subseteq\mathfrak n\widehat D=\ker\pi_D$ since $N\geq1$.

The local map $h_{\mathfrak p}:C\to D$ induces a unital map of fields $\bar h:C/\mathfrak m\to D/\mathfrak n$. It is injective: if a nonzero $v$ mapped to zero, then $1=\bar h(vv^{-1})=0$. The coordinate formula in [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion-map-local] gives $\pi_D\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}=\bar h\pi_C$. Thus $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}(x)$ belongs to $\ker\pi_D$ if and only if $x$ belongs to $\ker\pi_C$. The same formula at every coordinate gives $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}(\iota_C(c))=\iota(h_{\mathfrak p}(c))$; equality is coordinatewise by [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. In particular it respects the $R$-structure, since $h$ does.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, proof: the map B to A′ and the marked-point conclusion, with the omitted algebra written out

proof.text: Define $f:B\to\widehat D$ by $f(t)=\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}(\theta(t/1))$ and $g:B\to\widehat D$ by $g(t)=\iota(\phi(t)/1)$. These are $R$-algebra maps by the preceding step. Their composites from $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ to $\widehat D/J$ agree on each generator by the given congruences. They agree on coefficients because they are $R$-algebra maps, so the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] makes these composites equal. The quotient map has kernel $J$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Consequently $f(\overline H)-g(\overline H)\in J$ for every $H$, and hence $f(t)-g(t)\in J$ for every $t\in B$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, proof: the map B to A′ and the marked-point conclusion, with the omitted algebra written out

proof.text: For $t\in B$, $t/1$ belongs to $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$ exactly when $t\in\mathfrak q$: a fraction with numerator in $\mathfrak q$ is in the extended ideal, and conversely clearing the finitely many denominators in an expression in this ideal gives $st\in\mathfrak q$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak q$, whence $t\in\mathfrak q$ by primality. The same observation applies to $A',\mathfrak p'$. Locality of $\theta$ and step 3 now give $t\in\mathfrak q\iff\theta(t/1)\in\ker\pi_C\iff f(t)\in\ker\pi_D$. Since $f(t)-g(t)\in J\subseteq\ker\pi_D$, this is equivalent to $g(t)\in\ker\pi_D$. The residue compatibility of the completion map in [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] identifies the latter condition with $\phi(t)/1\in\mathfrak n$, equivalently $\phi(t)\in\mathfrak p'$. This proves $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak q$.

otin\mathfrak p'$. If $r/s=r'/s'$, the fraction relation in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] supplies $u
otin\mathfrak q$ with $u(rs'-r' s)=0$. Applying $\phi$ and cancelling the unit $\phi(u)/1$ in $D$ proves equality of the two proposed images. The sum and product rules for fractions prove this is an $R$-algebra homomorphism extending $\phi$. A fraction is in the extended prime exactly when its numerator is in the prime, by the preceding clearing-denominators argument. Therefore $\phi_{\mathfrak q}(r/s)\in\mathfrak n\iff\phi(r)\in\mathfrak p'\iff r\in\mathfrak q\iff r/s\in\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$; the map is local.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, proof: the map B to A′ and the marked-point conclusion, with the omitted algebra written out

proof.text: Write an arbitrary $z\in B_{\mathfrak q}$ as $r/s$ with $s\notin\mathfrak q$. Put $U=f(s)$ and $V=g(s)$. The element $U$ is a unit because $s/1$ is a unit in $B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $f$ extends through $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}\theta$; $V$ is a unit because $\phi(s)/1$ is a unit in $D$. Step 4 gives $f(r)-g(r)\in J$ and $U-V\in J$. In the commutative ring $\widehat D$, the explicit identity $f(r)U^{-1}-g(r)V^{-1}=(f(r)-g(r))U^{-1}+g(r)(V-U)U^{-1}V^{-1}$ shows that the difference belongs to $J$. The first term on the left is $\widehat h_{\mathfrak p}(\theta(z))$ and the second is $\iota(\phi_{\mathfrak q}(z))$, because homomorphisms preserve inverses of units. This is the required congruence for every fraction.

The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to live; only proof, proof_deps, searches and split_report were added. There are no new nodes, no re-split note, no SGA, no cycle, and live is still unsplit. Step 1: polynomial evaluation factors through (F); uniqueness via mv-ring algHom_ext; iterated vs mv ring identified as elementary. Step 2: C=A_p and D=A'_{p'} are local Noetherian (localization-noetherian), mĈ=ker π_C and nD̂=ker π_D, so J⊆nD̂ since N≥1. Step 3: h_p is local by h^{-1}(p′)=p; the residue map is injective; the coordinate formula of fs-adic-completion-map-local gives π_D ĥ = h̄ π_C and ĥι_C = ιh_p, so ĥ is an R-algebra map. Step 4: the two maps B→D̂/J agree on generators, so by mv uniqueness f−g∈J. Step 5: clearing denominators plus primality; θ local, step 3 and J⊆ker π_D give φ^{-1}(p′)=q as an equality. Step 6: φ_q is well defined via the u(rs′−r′s)=0 relation (zero divisors handled correctly) and is local by the numerator criterion. Step 7: I verified the identity (f−g)U^{-1}+g(V−U)U^{-1}V^{-1} = fU^{-1}−gV^{-1}, and both terms are in J. The parent's step 3 uses exactly these outputs. Edge cases: n=0 and m=0 work; non-injective h and θ are fine; the N=0 counterexample (k[T], q=(T), b=1) shows the N≥1 hypothesis is needed and it is present. Duplicate search with rg -L for 0CAU and phi^{-1}(p') found only the parent and siblings, none of which states this fact.
